enzyme_name: Aurachin B dehydrogenase (AuaH)
organism_context: Stigmatella aurantiaca (myxobacterium), aurachin biosynthetic cluster
rationale: EC 1.1.1.394 is AuaH, a short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase that performs the single NAD(H)-dependent redox step converting aurachin C to aurachin B; no second catalytic activity is reported for it in the aurachin literature.
direction_note: The KEGG/IUBMB record for EC 1.1.1.394 states explicitly that its equation is written non-physiologically and that the enzyme runs right-to-left (reducing the 4-hydroxy-3-oxo compound to the 3,4-diol, which then dehydrates spontaneously to aurachin B) - exactly ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: unidentified step of ipecac (emetine) alkaloid biosynthesis converting the 6,7-O,O-dimethyl-N-deacetylisoipecoside aglycone to protoemetine
organism_context: Carapichea ipecacuanha / Alangium salviifolium (MetaCyc PWY-7135, largely predicted)
rationale: No protein has been assigned to this MetaCyc step; the recent pathway elucidation shows the 1S branch proceeds to protoemetine but does not place a single enzyme on this exact aglycone-to-protoemetine conversion, which also loses C2O3 unaccounted for in the ModelSEED equation.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux in ipecac alkaloid formation runs toward protoemetine (left-to-right here), so the LLM's '>' matches the pathway even though the equation itself does not balance.

enzyme_name: Psilocybin synthase / norbaeocystin N-methyltransferase (PsiM)
organism_context: Psilocybe cubensis and other Psilocybe spp.
rationale: PsiM is a single-domain SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase that performs the final methylation of baeocystin to psilocybin; its two successive methylations (norbaeocystin to baeocystin to psilocybin) are the same catalytic activity, not two distinct ones.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible in the SAM-to-SAH direction, i.e. baeocystin + SAM to psilocybin + SAH, which is the LLM's '>'.

enzyme_name: Galactogen 6-beta-galactosyltransferase (UDP-galactose:galactogen beta-1,6-D-galactosyltransferase, EC 2.4.1.205)
organism_context: Helix pomatia albumen gland (snail); enzyme characterised only in crude/partially purified preparations, no sequence
rationale: The activity was identified in Helix pomatia albumen gland extracts in 1989 and has never been purified to a defined polypeptide or sequenced, so there is no usable evidence either way on mono- versus multifunctionality.
direction_note: Both the galactogen acceptor and the galactosylated product are absent from the ModelSEED entry, leaving 'UDP-Gal => UDP'; the real glycosyl transfer consumes UDP-Gal and releases UDP, i.e. the LLM's '>'.

enzyme_name: Tetrachlorohydroquinone reductive dehalogenase (PcpC), thiol-disulfide exchange half-reaction
organism_context: Sphingobium (Sphingomonas) chlorophenolicum, pentachlorophenol degradation
rationale: PcpC catalyses maleylacetone isomerisation at a rate close to a bona fide bacterial maleylacetoacetate isomerase in addition to its reductive dehalogenase chemistry, two genuinely distinct catalytic activities on one polypeptide; this reaction is its final thiol-disulfide exchange step releasing 2,6-dichlorohydroquinone and GSSG.
direction_note: GSSG (the exact C20H25N6O12S2 residual) is missing from the product side; with it restored the enzyme-catalysed step is GSH + S-glutathionyl conjugate to 2,6-dichlorohydroquinone + GSSG, the LLM's '>', and thiol-disulfide exchange with GSH excess makes it effectively one-way.

enzyme_name: Echinocandin B deacylase (ECB deacylase / aculeacin A acylase, AAC)
organism_context: Actinoplanes utahensis NRRL 12052; Ntn-hydrolase alpha/beta heterodimer autoprocessed from a single precursor
rationale: A single acyl-peptide hydrolase activity cleaves the N-acyl side chain from echinocandin B and its analogues including cilofungin; the two subunits come from autoproteolysis of one precursor, which the protocol treats as monofunctional, not bifunctional.
direction_note: The enzyme is a hydrolase: it deacylates cilofungin to the echinocandin B nucleus plus 4-(octyloxy)benzoate, which is ModelSEED's '<'; the LLM's '>' would be amide bond synthesis from a free carboxylate with no activated acyl donor, and neither the water nor the released acyl group appears in the equation.

enzyme_name: ToxD (toxoflavin biosynthesis protein; condensation of 5-amino-6-ribitylaminouracil with glycine to 1,6-didemethyltoxoflavin)
organism_context: Burkholderia glumae tox operon; homologue PFL1035 in Pseudomonas protegens Pf-5
rationale: ToxD is the single tox-operon protein assigned to the ARP + glycine condensation that builds the pyrimido-triazine core, and its crystal structure and active-site mutagenesis describe one active site with one chemistry; the downstream dual-specificity methyltransferase ToxA is a different protein.
direction_note: Toxoflavin biosynthesis runs ARP + glycine to 1,6-didemethyltoxoflavin (the LLM's '>'); the ribityl-derived leaving group is simply absent from the ModelSEED equation, which is why the group-contribution dG for this entry is nonsensically large.

enzyme_name: dTDP-3-amino-2,3,6-trideoxyhexose N,N-dimethyltransferase of the DesVI/TylM1 family
organism_context: Actinomycete deoxyaminosugar (desosamine/mycaminose/rhodosamine-type) biosynthesis; enzyme identity inferred from the chemistry and the characterised DesVI/TylM1 family
rationale: The chemistry (SAM-dependent conversion of a dTDP-3-N-methylamino-4-keto-trideoxyhexose to the N,N-dimethyl sugar) is the signature DesVI/TylM1 dimethyltransferase step; these enzymes perform both methylations at one active site, which is a single catalytic activity rather than bifunctionality.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer runs SAM to SAH, i.e. the monomethyl sugar to the dimethyl sugar (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require SAH to remethylate SAM.

enzyme_name: hydrolysis of the C4 ketimine of GDP-4-keto-3,6-dideoxymannose (release step downstream of ColD, GDP-4-keto-6-deoxy-D-mannose-3-dehydratase)
organism_context: GDP-L-colitose biosynthesis in Escherichia coli / Yersinia pseudotuberculosis; the PMP-dependent dehydratase ColD generates the imine
rationale: MetaCyc splits the ColD transformation and this entry is only the imine-to-ketone hydrolysis that releases ammonia; imine hydrolysis of this kind is normally spontaneous, and no protein is assigned to it separately, so the catalysing enzyme (if any) is unknown.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of a ketimine to the ketone plus free ammonia is essentially irreversible in dilute aqueous solution and is the direction the colitose pathway requires, i.e. the LLM's '>'.

enzyme_name: L-ascorbate peroxidase (APX, EC 1.11.1.11)
organism_context: class I haem peroxidase of plants, algae and some bacteria (MetaCyc L-ascorbate degradation II/III/V)
rationale: Ascorbate peroxidase is a single-activity class I haem peroxidase (the bifunctional member of that superfamily is catalase-peroxidase KatG, a different protein); called from established knowledge, no literature search needed.
direction_note: The oxidised ascorbate product is missing (the residual is exactly C6H6O6, dehydroascorbate); peroxidases reduce H2O2 to water irreversibly, so the LLM's '>' is right and ModelSEED's '<' would have water generating H2O2.

enzyme_name: unassigned ATP-dependent gamma-glutamyl ligase extending the APMF-Glu side chain to methanofuran b
organism_context: methanogenic archaea (MetaCyc PWY-5254); the characterised counterparts are the methylofuran polyglutamate ligases MyfA/MyfB (OrfY/Orf5) of Methylorubrum extorquens, while MfnA-MfnF of Methanocaldococcus jannaschii only build the APMF-Glu core
rationale: The six identified methanofuran genes (MfnA-MfnF) stop at the APMF-Glu core; the enzyme that adds the further glutamates to give methanofuran b has not been identified in methanogens, and the methylotroph glutamate ligases MyfA/MyfB are only functionally, not structurally, characterised.
direction_note: Written as a bare condensation releasing water with no ATP, the equation looks hydrolysis-favoured; the real ligation is ATP-driven and runs biosynthetically toward methanofuran b, i.e. the LLM's '>'.

enzyme_name: cytosolic glutathione S-transferase (generic CDNB-conjugating GST)
organism_context: generic MetaCyc GST-RXN - the standard 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene assay reaction, catalysed by essentially all soluble GST classes rather than one named protein
rationale: The canonical soluble GST activity exercised here is a single glutathione-conjugation chemistry; some classes carry extra activities (omega-class thiol transferase/dehydroascorbate reductase, MGST1 peroxidase) but no single enzyme is specified by this generic entry, so the conjugation activity alone is the honest call.
direction_note: The S-(2,4-dinitrophenyl)glutathione product is missing (the residual matches cpd08051 exactly); aromatic nucleophilic substitution with chloride loss is irreversible, so the LLM's '>' is correct.

enzyme_name: Diadinoxanthin de-epoxidase (DDE), a violaxanthin de-epoxidase-family lipocalin
organism_context: diatoms and haptophytes (e.g. Phaeodactylum tricornutum), thylakoid lumen, diadinoxanthin cycle
rationale: DDE is a VDE-type lipocalin carrying a single ascorbate-dependent de-epoxidation activity; the opposite reaction of the xanthophyll cycle is run by a physically separate FAD/NADPH/O2-dependent epoxidase.
direction_note: Dehydroascorbate (residual C6H6O6) is missing; because de-epoxidation and epoxidation are catalysed by two different enzymes with different cosubstrates, the ascorbate-coupled reaction only runs diadinoxanthin to diatoxanthin, the LLM's '>'.

enzyme_name: unassigned N-acyltransferase of the rhbABCDEF cluster that acylates the schizokinen core to rhizobactin 1021
organism_context: Sinorhizobium meliloti 2011/1021, rhizobactin 1021 siderophore biosynthesis
rationale: The rhb cluster was defined genetically but no individual gene product has been assigned to the hydroxamate N-acylation that distinguishes rhizobactin 1021 from schizokinen, so neither the protein nor its functionality can be fixed.
direction_note: Acyl transfer in vivo uses an activated acyl-ACP/acyl-CoA donor, but the equation uses a free fatty acid, which makes the written condensation look uphill; the biosynthetic direction is core + acyl to rhizobactin 1021, the LLM's '>'.

enzyme_name: Tyramine beta-monooxygenase / tyramine beta-hydroxylase (TBH, TbetaH)
organism_context: insects and other invertebrates (Drosophila melanogaster, Rhodnius prolixus, Laodelphax striatellus); copper-containing DBH/PHM family
rationale: TBH is the single-activity copper monooxygenase that beta-hydroxylates tyramine to octopamine using O2 and ascorbate; no second catalytic activity is attributed to it.
direction_note: Dehydroascorbate (residual C6H6O6) is missing; O2-consuming hydroxylation is irreversible, so tyramine to octopamine (the LLM's '>') is the only direction the enzyme runs.

enzyme_name: none - the Painter reaction is the non-enzymatic reduction of selenite by glutathione
organism_context: chemical reaction in any GSH-containing cytosol; downstream reduction of selenodiglutathione is enzymatic (glutathione reductase/thioredoxin reductase) but this step is not
rationale: Selenite undergoes multistep non-enzymatic reduction by glutathione to selenodiglutathione (Painter reaction); there is no catalysing protein, so no functionality can be assigned.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the products (residual matches cpd00111); the chemistry runs selenite + GSH to selenodiglutathione, i.e. the LLM's '>', and being non-enzymatic the direction is purely thermodynamic.

enzyme_name: Desulfo-A47934 sulfotransferase (StaL, EC 2.8.2.36)
organism_context: Streptomyces toyocaensis NRRL 15009, A47934 glycopeptide biosynthesis
rationale: StaL is a PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase of known structure catalysing the single final sulfonation of the A47934 aglycone; no additional catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: Sulfotransferases run PAPS + acceptor to PAP + sulfated acceptor, which is left-to-right here (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require PAP to regenerate PAPS.

enzyme_name: none identified - spontaneous hydrolysis of the N-methyl aldimine of 4-hydroxyphenylacetaldehyde
organism_context: MetaCyc RXN-15194, no pathway assignment in the ModelSEED entry; such imines are the typical released products of flavin amine oxidases acting on N-methyltyramine
rationale: No protein is assigned to this MetaCyc reaction and aldimine hydrolysis of this kind proceeds spontaneously in water, so the catalysing enzyme is honestly unknown.
direction_note: Imine hydrolysis to the aldehyde plus free methylamine is strongly favoured in dilute aqueous solution (the LLM's '>'); the reverse condensation only occurs at high amine concentration.

enzyme_name: none identified - intramolecular transesterification (lactonisation) of the diphenyl ether meta-cleavage product
organism_context: bacterial diphenyl ether degradation (Sphingomonas sp. SS3 and relatives, MetaCyc PWY-7747)
rationale: The ring-fission product is a phenyl ester whose 2-enol oxygen closes onto the ester carbonyl, expelling phenolate; this is facile uncatalysed chemistry and no enzyme is assigned to the step, consistent with phenol appearing as a free intermediate during diphenyl ether degradation.
direction_note: Lactone formation with expulsion of a phenolate leaving group is effectively irreversible (the LLM's '>'), and even the group-contribution estimate agrees with '>' here; ModelSEED's '<' would require phenol to attack the pyrone.

enzyme_name: Glutathione oxidase (EC 1.8.3.3), an FAD flavoprotein thiol oxidase
organism_context: fungal/bacterial thiol oxidase; also acts slowly on L-cysteine and other thiols
rationale: A single FAD-dependent thiol oxidase activity (2 GSH + O2 to GSSG + H2O2) with broadened thiol specificity, which is substrate promiscuity rather than a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the products (residual matches cpd00111); flavin thiol oxidases reduce O2 to H2O2 irreversibly, so the LLM's '>' is correct and ModelSEED's '<' would have H2O2 reducing GSSG.

enzyme_name: none - non-enzymatic thiol-disulfide (sulfane sulfur) exchange between hydrogen sulfide and glutathione disulfide
organism_context: sulfide oxidation via persulfide dioxygenase (MetaCyc PWY-5285); the enzymatic steps of that pathway are sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase upstream and ETHE1/persulfide dioxygenase downstream, not this exchange
rationale: Glutathione persulfide is formed from sulfide and GSSG by direct nucleophilic thiol-disulfide exchange with no catalyst; there is therefore no enzyme whose functionality could be classified.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the product side; restoring it makes ModelSEED's '<' read H2S + GSSG to GSH + GSSH, the persulfide-forming direction the sulfide-oxidation pathway requires, whereas the LLM's '>' would run persulfide back to sulfide - though the exchange is near-isoergonic and really pool-driven.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous attack of glutathione on the N-hydroxysulfenamide GSNHOH (the product of GSNO reduction by ADH5/GSNOR)
organism_context: protein S-nitrosylation/denitrosylation (MetaCyc PWY-7798); the upstream S-nitrosoglutathione reductase ADH5 is itself bifunctional (formaldehyde dehydrogenase + GSNO reductase) but does not catalyse this step
rationale: GSNHOH generated by ADH5/GSNOR reacts rapidly and non-enzymatically with a second glutathione to give GSSG and hydroxylamine, so no enzyme catalyses this particular reaction.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the products (residual matches cpd00111); the chemistry is a one-way thiol attack giving GSSG + NH2OH, the LLM's '>', and ModelSEED's '<' would have hydroxylamine attacking GSSG to regenerate the N-hydroxysulfenamide.

enzyme_name: Tyrosinase / polyphenol oxidase (monophenolase activity on portulacaxanthin II)
organism_context: plant and fungal tyrosinases acting on betaxanthins (betalain biosynthesis via dopaxanthin, MetaCyc PWY-5404)
rationale: A single binuclear-copper polypeptide carries two distinct catalytic activities - hydroxylation of monophenols and oxidation of o-diphenols to quinones - and both were demonstrated on betaxanthin substrate pairs including the tyrosine-betaxanthin/DOPA-betaxanthin couple.
direction_note: Dehydroascorbate (residual C6H6O6) is missing; the enzyme's bifunctionality is exactly what makes this one-way - the monophenolase activity hydroxylates portulacaxanthin II to dopaxanthin (the LLM's '>') and the diphenolase activity then consumes the dopaxanthin, so there is no return flux.

enzyme_name: Hydroxysqualene dehydroxylase (HpnE, EC 1.17.8.1)
organism_context: Rhodopseudomonas palustris and Zymomonas mobilis; third enzyme of the bacterial HpnD/HpnC/HpnE route from farnesyl diphosphate to squalene (hopanoid biosynthesis)
rationale: HpnE is an amine-oxidase-family flavoprotein with the single activity of reductively removing the hydroxyl from hydroxysqualene to give squalene; the two other steps of the bacterial squalene route are separate proteins (HpnD, HpnC).
direction_note: The IUBMB/KEGG equation for EC 1.17.8.1 is written squalene-first but the record states the enzyme physiologically produces squalene, i.e. hydroxysqualene + FADH2 to squalene + FAD + H2O - exactly ModelSEED's '<'; the LLM's '>' is the non-physiological hydroxylating direction.

enzyme_name: Olivetol synthase / tetraketide synthase (CsTKS, OLS), a type III polyketide synthase - derailment release of the triketide pyrone
organism_context: Cannabis sativa olivetolic acid/olivetol biosynthesis (MetaCyc PWY-7105)
rationale: The triketide pyrone PDAL is a derailment product of the iterative type III PKS, formed by lactonisation of the enzyme-bound 3,5-dioxodecanoyl intermediate with CoA release; the PKS has one iterative condensation activity and the lactonisation itself is a spontaneous, uncatalysed release.
direction_note: Intramolecular lactonisation expelling CoA thiolate is irreversible (the LLM's '>', which group contribution also supports); ModelSEED's '<' would require free CoA to re-open the pyrone into a beta-diketo thioester, which does not happen.
